Description: Intrinsic motivation during online learning, 22 items on a 1-7 scale, answered by 1,635 Indonesian students across two samples. Covariates: cov_gender, cov_age, cov_semester, cov_faculty, cov_level, cov_study.
Reference: Agusta, E. (2023). Dataset of Intrinsic Motivation Students while Online Learning in South Sumatera, Indonesia [Dataset]. Mendeley Data.
Notes: The two workbooks are the same instrument on two samples and are merged under cov_study. The header is split across two rows -- section names in row 0, item numbers 1-22 in row 1 -- so the item columns are found by their numbering rather than sliced at a fixed offset, which differs between the files. One row with demographics and no item response at all is dropped; no row is partially answered.

Description: A Digital Health Literacy Scale for undergraduates, 13 items in four subscale blocks on a 1-5 scale, answered by 1,292 Chinese students. Covariates: cov_gender, cov_education_level, cov_region, cov_use_frequency.
Reference: Cao, H., & Chen, P.-F. (2026). Anonymized survey dataset of Digital Health Literacy Scale for Chinese Undergraduate Students [Dataset]. figshare.
Notes: One table rather than four: this is the validation sample for one instrument and the four prefixes (DCE, IU, IE, AA) are its subscales, which the deposit never expands, so naming four constructs would be a guess. The prefix stays in the item code. The observed range is 2-5 of a permitted 1-5.

Description: The UEF-1 executive-function self-report, 31 items on a 1-5 scale, answered by 1,092 Cuban university students. Covariates: cov_age, cov_sex, cov_province.
Reference: Díaz Guerra, D. D., Ramos-Galarza, C., Hernández Lugo, M. de la C., & Broche-Pérez, Y. (2024). Validity and Reliability of the Executive Function Scale (UEF-1) in Cuban University Students [Dataset]. Mendeley Data.
Notes: No item text is possible from this deposit: 0 of its 41 variable labels carry a stem, and the populated value labels are option text alone, which irw#1770 forbids shipping. The deposit's F1-F7 factor scores are not shipped.

Description: A 27-item dichotomous Internet Gaming Disorder pool answered by 8,662 Chinese college students, shipped with the study's own 27x9 Q-matrix in qmatrix1-qmatrix9. Covariates: none.
Reference: Liu, S. (2024). Assessing the Diagnostic Precision of the Internet Gaming Disorder Scale (IGD-27) Using Diagnostic Classification Models: An Exploratory Study [Dataset]. figshare.
Notes: The Q-matrix maps each item to one of the nine DSM-5 IGD criteria, three items per criterion, joined to the items by row order because that is the only correspondence the deposit provides (IGD_Q.csv has no item column); the script asserts both shapes and the single-attribute structure. The rights register blocks the IGDS9-SF's wording, which does not reach this table: no wording is deposited and response data ships regardless (irw_validate/rights.py).

Description: The Body Appreciation Scale, 10 items on a 1-7 scale, answered by 961 Chinese adolescents (study 2). Covariates: cov_age, cov_gender, cov_grade, cov_origin, cov_social_media_use.
Reference: Liu, X., Zhang, K., Cao, Y., & Chen, S. (2025). Social Media Use, Body Image, and Self-Esteem Among Chinese Adolescents: Experimental and Survey Data (N = 1,113) [Dataset]. figshare.
Notes: The deposit's BASsum equals the block sum for all 961 respondents. Only the first column of each block carries a label, and it names the instrument rather than the item, so no item text is extractable.

Description: A self-esteem scale, 10 items on a 1-4 scale, answered before and after an image-exposure manipulation by 152 Chinese middle-school students (study 1). Covariates: cov_age, cov_gender, cov_grade, cov_origin, cov_social_media_use, cov_group.
Reference: Liu, X., Zhang, K., Cao, Y., & Chen, S. (2025). Social Media Use, Body Image, and Self-Esteem Among Chinese Adolescents: Experimental and Survey Data (N = 1,113) [Dataset]. figshare.
Notes: Two waves on `wave`: the deposit's B* and G* blocks share the label "Self-Esteem Scale" and the same four value labels, and its pre- and post-test totals equal the B and G sums respectively for all 152 respondents, which is what identifies which block is which. Two responses coded 7 on a 1-4 scale are dropped as out of range; the deposit's own totals include them, which is one reason no total is shipped. cov_group is the 2x2 image condition (38 respondents per cell).

Description: A self-esteem scale, 10 items on a 1-5 scale, answered by 961 Chinese adolescents (study 2). Covariates: cov_age, cov_gender, cov_grade, cov_origin, cov_social_media_use.
Reference: Liu, X., Zhang, K., Cao, Y., & Chen, S. (2025). Social Media Use, Body Image, and Self-Esteem Among Chinese Adolescents: Experimental and Survey Data (N = 1,113) [Dataset]. figshare.
Notes: The deposit's SEsum equals the block sum for all 961 respondents. Labelled only "SE" at the block level; almost certainly the RSES but the deposit does not say.

Description: Adaptability, 9 items on a 1-5 scale, answered twice by 1,192 English students aged 16-19. Covariates: cov_school, cov_gender, cov_age, cov_ethnicity.
Reference: Putwain, D. (2022). Test Anxiety, Wellbeing, Buoyancy, Adaptability, and Mental Health Risk [Dataset]. Mendeley Data.
Notes: Two waves on `wave` (the deposit's unprefixed columns are time 1, its T2* columns the same items at time 2), with the item name carrying no wave so one item links across both. Description: The Emotion Regulation Questionnaire, 10 items on a 1-7 scale, answered in Spanish by 1,317 Peruvian university students. Covariates: cov_sex, cov_age, cov_programme, cov_university.
